data.name: Bhartihari
data.gender_notes: Bhartihari is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bharti means 'to reside' and Hari means 'God, Lord Vishnu'. Bhartihari refers to the one who resides on the earth as the divine being. He is also known as Bhartrihari, a great sage in Hindu mythology. The name Bhartihari carries the meaning “Lord of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhartihari usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Bhartihari belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhartihari total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Bhartihari is an ancient name that holds significant cultural importance in India, particularly among scholars, sages, and devotees. It reflects a strong connection to the land and signifies the desire to reside on earth as a divine and enlightened being, contributing to the betterment of society. The name is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and has been used by several revered figures, including the great sage Bhartrihari.
data.spiritual_significance: Bhartihari is a powerful spiritual name that embodies the quest for self-realization and God-realization (Bhagavan or God) simultaneously. It encourages the belief that one can attain divine consciousness by immersing oneself in the present moment and connecting with the divine energy that resides in all beings. This name inspires selflessness, inner peace, and a deep sense of connection with the divine, fostering spiritual growth and development in those who bear it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhartihari: Dweller in the heart of God. Deep devotee, surrendering all actions to the divine will.
